# Tisonik — Public Product Reference

Tisonik is operated by TSquare Ventures LLC, a Wyoming (USA) limited liability company. Tisonik provides guest-experience activation for cruise lines and all-inclusive hotels and resorts. It is designed as a white-label interaction layer inside an operator's existing digital journey rather than as a separate consumer destination.

## All-inclusive hotels and resorts

### Experience discovery and participation
- Tisonik can help guests find included dining, activities, entertainment, sports, wellness and resort programming while they are on property.
- Included and premium experiences should be clearly distinguished so guests understand what is already part of the stay and what costs extra.
- Discovery can use time and resort context so the experience is more useful than one static catalogue.

### In-stay ratings and service recovery
- The resort can invite guests to rate the stay while they are still on property or shortly before departure, when there is still time to act on poor experiences.
- The rating flow is designed to take no more than about five minutes.
- The rating product uses exactly 10 standard questions. Participating hotels do not choose, replace or rewrite the questions.
- Questions 1–8 are fixed guest pain-point questions, each using the same 1–10 score scale.
- Those eight scored areas cover room cleanliness and maintenance, room comfort, food quality and choice, drinks and bar service, waiting times and speed of service, staff helpfulness and welcome, pools/beach/shared areas, and ease of finding and joining activities, entertainment and included experiences.
- Question 9 is “What was good?” and allows up to 400 characters.
- Question 10 is “What could be improved?” and allows up to 400 characters.
- A poor or concerning in-stay rating can be routed into a service-recovery workflow so the resort can acknowledge, resolve and follow up before checkout where possible.
- Participation means publication: submitted ratings go public, and a participating property cannot selectively suppress or hold back a rating because it is poor.
- Service recovery does not remove the submitted rating from the publication path.

### Staff recognition
- Tisonik can give guests a simple way to recognize resort employees who made the stay better.
- The resort use case is positive recognition, not a public employee leaderboard.

### Ancillary revenue and premium experience discovery
- The commercial opportunity extends beyond a single upsell or static catalogue.
- Relevant paid experiences can include spa and wellness, speciality dining, excursions, private transfers, cabanas and daybeds, watersports, celebrations and other resort-specific experiences.
- Tisonik can surface these opportunities at useful moments inside the guest journey while clearly distinguishing paid experiences from what is already included.
- Tisonik does not need to own the resort's inventory, availability, pricing, checkout, payment or fulfilment. Those remain with the resort.
- Commercial performance claims should follow real pilot evidence and agreed attribution logic.

### Resort integration and pilot
- Tisonik is designed as an experience layer rather than a replacement for the resort's PMS, booking engine, guest app or commerce stack.
- A resort pilot can start with one property, selected guest journeys, an explicit integration boundary and success measures agreed before launch.
- Public resort demos and metrics are illustrative and do not imply an affiliation with any hotel or resort brand or evidence of production performance.

## Cruise product areas

### Passenger experience
- The cruise line may include CruiseConnect recognition as a clearly stated purpose in its adult boarding imaging enrolment. Adults who accept are enrolled once for the sailing with no second Anonymous Vibe confirmation; adults who decline or opt out are excluded from matching.
- A sender photographs an intended adult receiver inside the cruise-line app. Operator-side recognition returns only an opaque one-time token or unavailable result—never a name, profile, candidate list, match score or rejection reason.
- Children cannot send, receive or be matched for passenger vibes. Same-cabin/booking-group and duplicate attempts are rejected operator-side.
- The capture is discarded after matching. Compliments use prepared blocks, contain no sender identity and are delivered after randomized delay or in a batch.
- Dense ranking gives equal valid-vibe totals the same position; Top Five means the first five score positions, not necessarily five passengers. The card is private and only its passenger may share it.
- Event RSVP is count-only by default. A passenger may separately show a chosen name/image to confirmed attendees.

### Crew recognition
- Guests frame the crew member and visible badge while the service moment is fresh.
- When duplicate names make text insufficient, the operator's identity service may perform face matching under its own approved biometric controls.
- Images, biometric templates, candidate lists and match scores remain on-device, ship-local or in cruise-line systems; Tisonik never receives them.
- Recognition uses prepared positive reasons and avoids public crew rankings.

### Service recovery
- Guests receive a private route to signal friction during the sailing.
- Experience Pulse supports timely service feedback and outcome measurement.

### Engagement and ancillary discovery
- Voluntary interests and onboard context can surface relevant activities or experiences.
- The cruise line retains inventory, pricing, checkout, payment and fulfilment.
- Live-event feedback uses three to five structured questions and prepared response blocks without free text.
- Authorized leaders receive immediate aggregate feedback; the cruise line controls publication.

### Aggregate-only measurement
- The default cruise architecture has no Tisonik passenger/crew source-event analytics endpoint.
- A cruise-line or ship-local privacy gateway sends only a predefined aggregate report covering activation, recognition, structured ratings, recovery and net attributed revenue.
- Names, passenger or crew identifiers, photos, booking/attribution references, exact event timestamps, free text and payment data cannot enter that report.
- Randomized or hashed person-level identifiers are also excluded because pseudonymous data may remain personal data.
- Non-identifying service-health totals may include uptime, latency buckets, sync success, deployed version and error counts.
- The default minimum reporting group is 20; smaller cells are suppressed or rolled up before transmission.

## Product and evidence boundaries
- Tisonik is not a hotel operator, cruise operator, booking engine or merchant.
- Public demonstrations and demo metrics are illustrative and do not imply an operator affiliation.
- Performance claims should follow real pilot evidence.
- Integration, data, privacy and deployment details must be agreed with each operator for a real implementation.
